samples.summary: Only the frozen-ROW branch of the new `crossesFreezePane` guard is tested; the frozen-column branch has no test anywhere
samples.evidence: The new helper `crossesFreezePane` (sheet.ts:2491) has two independent branches (`crossesRows`, `crossesCols`) and two call sites (`planPasteMerges` at sheet.ts:2420 and `canMergeSelection` at sheet.ts:4653). The only new test, 'should refuse a paste that lands a block across a frozen row' (merge.test.ts:621), calls `setFreezePane(2, 0)` — frozenCols is 0, so the `crossesCols` branch is never evaluated as true and would pass even if the column comparison were wrong (e.g. `>=`/`>` swapped or `.r` used instead of `.c`). Grepping `packages/sheets/test` for `setFreezePane` shows only freeze-pane.test.ts (which asserts freeze bookkeeping, never merging) and this one merge test. Result: a broken frozen-column guard would ship silently, letting a paste (and, via `canMergeSelection`, the merge button) create a block straddling a frozen column — exactly what the renderer is documented to assume cannot happen.

samples.summary: `canMergeSelection`'s freeze-boundary rule, now delegated to the shared `crossesFreezePane` helper, has no test at either call site
samples.evidence: The delta replaces the inline frozen-row/col check in `canMergeSelection` with `this.crossesFreezePane(selection)`. The only tests touching `canMergeSelection` are pivot-protection.test.ts:132 (pivot sheets return false) — no test sets a freeze pane and asserts `canMergeSelection()` is false for a straddling selection. So the refactor's behaviour preservation at this call site is proved by nothing; a regression here silently re-enables a merge the product forbids. (Boundary semantics `<= frozenRows` / `> frozenRows` are also unasserted.)

samples.summary: `rangeOf` on an empty grid (returns ±Infinity bounds) is untested
samples.evidence: The rewritten `rangeOf` (coordinates.ts) seeds `Infinity`/`-Infinity` and returns them unchanged for an empty grid. The two new tests cover a 3-cell grid and a 200k-cell grid only; no test pins the empty-map result, so a later change to that degenerate contract would go unnoticed. Behaviour is unchanged from the previous `Math.min(...[])` implementation, hence nit rather than a gap in new behaviour.

mergedFrom.summary: New cut test does not assert the clipped source cells / stale data left behind by the moved block

finding.summary: No test that a CUT paste still refuses when it clips a merged block that is NOT part of the cut
finding.evidence: The delta weakens the split-guard for cuts (`planPasteMerges` filters `getMergesIntersecting(destRange)` by a `travelling` set when `isCut`). The only test covering the weakened path is the new one at merge.test.ts:528, which asserts the *non*-refusal direction (its own block). The one refusal test, 'should refuse a paste that would split a destination block' (merge.test.ts:476-502), uses `sheet.copy()`, so it exercises `isCut === false` only. I grepped every `sheet.cut()` call in packages/sheets/test (merge.test.ts:395, 540 and clipboard.test.ts) and none combines a cut with a destination that clips a foreign merged block. Consequence: if the exclusion were over-broad (e.g. skipping the check entirely for cuts, or a wrong anchor comparison), a cut paste would split a destination merge and corrupt the merge map with a green suite.

verdict.reason: The test the finding says is missing exists in the same file it points at. `packages/sheets/test/sheet/merge.test.ts:558-586`, "should refuse a cut that clips a block it does not move", merges C3:D3, then does `await sheet.cut()` on A3:B3 (line 572) and pastes at B3 so the destination B3:C3 clips the foreign C3:D3 block that is NOT part of the cut. It asserts `expect(refusals).toEqual(['merge-paste-partial'])` (line 579), that the foreign block survives intact (`merges.get('C3')` === {rs:1,cs:2}, size 1, lines 580-582) and that the refusal is whole — the cut source still holds '10' at A3 and C3 still holds '30' (lines 584-585). This exercises exactly the weakened branch at sheet.ts:2450-2456 (`travelling` filter applied when `isCut`): if the exclusion were over-broad (skipping the check for cuts, or a wrong anchor comparison), this test would fail because no refusal would be recorded and the C3:D3 block would be split. A second cut-side refusal test at merge.test.ts:588-619 covers the related case where the recorded block was unmerged/re-merged under the clipboard so it is no longer 'travelling', also asserting 'merge-paste-partial'. The finding's premise that "the one refusal test ... uses sheet.copy()" is factually wrong: grep for `merge-paste-partial` yields three assertions in this file (lines 496, 579, 615), two of which follow `sheet.cut()`.
